statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail risk remains in the low band at 14% while stress stays elevated at 55% on oil and geopolitical headline flow.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with a normal, range-respecting regime for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 12:30Z-15:00Z, spanning the jobless-claims and trade block, the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z ISM Services release. Conditional tail touches the watch band only in the 14:00Z hour and stays below the block threshold for every other hour of the forecast, including the pre-payrolls build late in the horizon.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a two-way overnight band before the US data block; tail low, stress elevated on firmer crude
body: NQ futures trade near 29,175, down about 0.04% against a 29,186.25 previous close, inside a 29,075-29,292.75 overnight band roughly 0.75% wide. Price rotated from the 29,292.75 high back below the previous close and has since recovered to mid-range, so meaningful mean reversion is present and no session extreme is being defended. Two independent quote sources agree on level, direction and day range. VIX is 15.27, up about 0.5% and low in absolute terms. Treasury yields have rolled over from Wednesday's three-year highs, with the 10Y at 4.777%, the 2Y at 4.37% and the 30Y at 5.25%, all marginally lower on the day. The clearest amplifier is energy: WTI is 92.54 dollars, up about 1.68%, and Brent is 96.64 dollars, with the ongoing US-Iran conflict keeping Strait of Hormuz shipping below half its ten-day average. That combination supports an elevated stress reading while leaving tail in the low band, because the observed price path still offers retracement rather than persistent one-way extension. Today's catalysts are the 12:30Z jobless-claims and trade block, the 13:45Z S&P Global services final and the 14:00Z ISM Services release, ahead of Friday's August payrolls. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was 294 minutes old at assessment time and therefore treated as stale; it was not used as evidence in this assessment.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours began in Wednesday's European-session downdraft, when tail reached 20% and stress 72% in a trend-down regime as long-end yields pushed to three-year highs. From roughly 12:00Z on 2 September the regime turned mixed and both scores decayed steadily through the US session and into the evening, with tail reaching 11% and stress the mid-50s. The Asian and European hours of 3 September have been a flat normal regime, tail holding 12-14% and stress drifting from the mid-50s down to 52% before ticking back up as crude firmed. Five hourly slots have no published assessment and are marked unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours contain one dense catalyst block and then a long decay into Friday's payrolls. Conditional tail steps up from 14% through the 12:00Z pre-release hour, peaks at 21% in the 14:00Z hour where ISM Services overlaps the first half hour of cash trade, then falls back into the low band from 15:00Z as the impulse is assumed to fade. The 19:00Z power hour is a secondary bump. Overnight hours hold 10-12% with unscheduled Middle East headlines as the residual amplifier, before a gradual pre-payrolls build through the European morning that reaches 17% in the final slot ahead of the 12:30Z employment block. Every forecast hour except 14:00Z maps to EA_ON; that single hour maps to WATCH. Forecast confidence decays with horizon by design.
